subject: Representing item parameters in matrix format

messages.author: 84aac2580b195c68
messages.subject: Representing item parameters in matrix format
parts:
Hello everyone,

Does anyone know some shortcut way of how to represent the coef(mod)
mod <- mirt(Science, 1, 'gpcm')
coef(mod)

in a matrix form with the columns representing the names of the parameters?






Thank you

messages.author: 70d0917afd869432
messages.subject: Re: Representing item parameters in matrix format
parts:
This is a bit hacky, especially because coef(mod) includes GroupPars, which has a length of 2 rather than 9 so I'm just filtering it out manually, but does something like this help?

coefs <- coef(mod)
coefs.m <- cbind(t(coefs[[1]]), t(coefs[[2]]), t(coefs[[3]]), t(coefs[[4]]))
colnames(coefs.m) <- names(coefs)[1:4]
as.matrix(coefs.m)

messages.author: 2d98f40c09e307a5
messages.subject: Re: Representing item parameters in matrix format
parts:
I had the same problem.  I used the mirt function mod2values and then wrote a little function using the reshape2 package function dcast.  This puts things in a dataframe.  the function acast would put it in an array.

Recast.m2v=function(df){
  tmp=mod2values(df)
  tmp=tmp[,c("item","name","value")]  #keeping just vars of interest
  tmp=tmp[1:(dim(tmp)[1]-2),] #stripping out group mean and cov
  tmp=tmp[tmp$name!="u",]  #all upperbounds of interest are 1 so this can be stripped too
  out=dcast(tmp,item~...)
  return(out)
}
